label: DrayTek Vigor 2765 VDSL2 / Ethernet WAN VPN router
description: DrayTek Vigor 2765 - SoHo VDSL2 and Ethernet WAN VPN router (base model: no Wi-Fi, no VoIP ports) with one RJ-11 VDSL2/VDSL2 35b/ADSL2+ WAN, four Gigabit Ethernet RJ-45 ports one of which can be reassigned as the Ethernet WAN2, two USB 2.0 ports, SPI firewall with content filtering, 2 LAN subnets with port-based or 802.1Q VLANs and two VPN tunnels. 950 Mbps firewall throughput on Ethernet WAN, 21.8 W maximum from a 12 V external supply.
notes: The series datasheet lists the sockets one by one: '**WAN1: VDSL2 / VDSL2 35b / ADSL2+, RJ-11**', '**WAN2/LAN Switchable Port: 1x Gigabit Ethernet, RJ-45**', '**LAN Ports: 4x Gigabit Ethernet, RJ-45 (3x with WAN2 enabled)**', '**WAN3: USB 2.0**'. That parenthetical is the modelling decision: the Ethernet WAN is **not a fifth socket** - it is one of the four, reassigned. So the spec declares `dsl0` plus four LAN ports and puts the reassignment in this note, rather than inventing a `wan2` that would make the box look like it has five RJ-45s. A lab that needs an Ethernet WAN should cable `lan4` and treat it as the uplink. The USB sockets are WAN-capable (3G/4G modem) but are not Ethernet, so they are described and not modelled. This is the base `-K` model: the datasheet's AC1300 radios belong to the 'ac' variants and the two FXS phone ports to 'Vac', so neither is declared here. No PoE in or out - 12 V external PSU.
